*denote-api.txt*  denote.nvim Lua API reference (generated, do not edit)

Generated from the LuaCATS annotations in lua/denote/ by `make docs`.
For the user guide, see |denote.txt|.

==============================================================================
Emacs Denote, rebuilt for Neovim in pure Lua                            *denote*

 File-naming-first note-taking for Neovim with zero dependencies, full
 Org mode (`org.nvim`), Markdown (YAML & TOML), and plain text support,
 backlinks, live query links, explorer, silos, daily journal, and
 Folgezettel sequences.

 `require("denote")` re-exports the commands of the modules below. Besides
 the functions listed here, `backlinks()`, `preview()`, `explorer()`, and
 `capture()` are the same as |denote.backlinks.open|, |denote.preview.open|,
 |denote.explorer.open|, and |denote.capture.capture|.

M.setup({opts?})                                                  *denote.setup*
     Initialize denote.nvim with user configuration.

    Parameters: ~
        {opts?}  (table)

    Returns: ~
        (denote.Config)

Configuration defaults and accessors                             *denote.config*

denote.FileTypeSpec                                        *denote.FileTypeSpec*

    Fields: ~
        {extension}             (string)                                                          File extension including leading dot (e.g. ".org", ".md")
        {front_matter}          (string|fun(meta:table):string)                                   Front matter template or builder
        {date_format?}          (string)                                                          os.date format or special token ("org", "iso8601", "date")
        {link_format?}          (string)                                                          Link template with %s placeholders (id, description)
        {link_id_only_format?}  (string)                                                          ID-only link template with %s placeholder (id)
        {parse?}                (fun(lines:string[]):denote.ParsedFrontMatter)                    Optional front matter parser for custom file types
        {rewrite?}              (fun(lines:string[],updates:table,opts?:table):string[],boolean)  Optional front matter rewriter for custom file types


denote.JournalConfig                                      *denote.JournalConfig*

    Fields: ~
        {directory?}     (string|nil)                       Directory for journal entries (nil -> <directory>/journal or <directory>)
        {keyword}        (string)                           Keyword tag added to journal entries
        {title_format?}  (string|table<string,string>|nil)  os.date format for titles; nil -> per-interval default, a table maps interval -> format
        {interval?}      ()


denote.SequenceConfig                                    *denote.SequenceConfig*

    Fields: ~
        {scheme}  ()


denote.MappingsConfig                                    *denote.MappingsConfig*

    Fields: ~
        {enabled}               (boolean)       Register default global keymaps
        {prefix}                (string)        Leader prefix for global keymaps (default: "<leader>n")
        {follow_link}           (string|false)  Buffer-local keymap to follow a denote: link (default: "<CR>")
        {follow_link_fallback}  (boolean)       Fall back to native keymap when cursor is not on a denote: link
        {preview_link}          (string|false)  Buffer-local keymap to preview the linked note (default: "K")

M.canonicalize({path})                              *denote.config.canonicalize*
     Resolve symlinks in `path` (e.g. macOS `/var` -> `/private/var`) so that paths built from
     the Denote directory compare equal to buffer names, which Neovim stores resolved.
     Non-existent trailing components are kept as-is on top of the nearest existing ancestor.

    Parameters: ~
        {path}  (string)

    Returns: ~
        (string)


M.directory({dir?})                                    *denote.config.directory*
     Return the currently active Denote directory (expanded and normalized).

    Parameters: ~
        {dir?}  (string)  Optional explicit directory override

    Returns: ~
        (string)


==============================================================================
Creating Denote notes (interactive prompts, templates, open-or-create, region)
                                                               *denote.create*

denote.CreateOpts                                            *denote.CreateOpts*

    Fields: ~
        {title?}           (string)
        {keywords?}        (string[]|string)
        {file_type?}       (string)
        {subdirectory?}    (string)                       Subdirectory relative to `dir` (or absolute path)
        {date?}            (string|integer)               Date string or Unix timestamp
        {template?}        (string)                       Template key from `config.opts.templates`
        {signature?}       (string)
        {body?}            (string)                       Extra body text appended after front matter / template
        {dir?}             (string)                       Explicit root directory override
        {open?}            (boolean)                      Open the created note in Neovim (default: true)
        {how?}             (string)                       Window open mode ("edit", "split", "vsplit", "tab")
        {save?}            (boolean)                      Override `save_buffer_after_creation`
        {prompts?}         (string[])                     Override prompt sequence for interactive creation
        {interactive?}     (boolean)                      When false, create synchronously without prompting
        {on_created?}      (fun(path:string,meta:table))  Callback after note is created
        {body_template?}   (string)                       Body with capture escapes (`%^{Prompt}`, `%i`, `%a`, `%?`, ...)
        {context?}         (denote.CaptureContext)        Capture context for template escapes (origin, region, answers)
        {_initial_title?}  (string)                       Internal: default text for the title prompt
        {_silo_dir?}       (string)                       Internal: create the note inside this silo
        {_region_code?}    ({text:string,ft:string})      Internal: code region wrapped after file_type is resolved


denote.RegionOpts : denote.CreateOpts                        *denote.RegionOpts*

    Fields: ~
        {line1?}  (integer)  First line of the region (default: `'<`)
        {line2?}  (integer)  Last line of the region (default: `'>`)


M.create_sync({opts})                                *denote.create.create_sync*
     Create a Denote note synchronously from resolved options (no prompts).
     Writes the file to disk (or opens it in a buffer if `save == false` and `open == true`),
     and returns `{ path, identifier, title, keywords, signature, file_type, date, bufnr }`.

    Parameters: ~
        {opts}  (denote.CreateOpts)

    Returns: ~
        (table)


M.note({opts?})                                             *denote.create.note*
     Primary note creation entry point (matching `M-x denote`).
     If `opts.title` is supplied along with `opts.interactive == false` (or `opts.open == false`),
     creates immediately without prompting; otherwise runs the configured `prompts` pipeline.

    Parameters: ~
        {opts?}  (denote.CreateOpts)

    Returns: ~
        (table|nil)


M.type({opts?})                                             *denote.create.type*
     Create a note prompting for file type (`denote-type`).

    Parameters: ~
        {opts?}  (denote.CreateOpts)


M.date({opts?})                                             *denote.create.date*
     Create a note prompting for custom date (`denote-date`).

    Parameters: ~
        {opts?}  (denote.CreateOpts)


M.subdirectory({opts?})                             *denote.create.subdirectory*
     Create a note prompting for subdirectory (`denote-subdirectory`).

    Parameters: ~
        {opts?}  (denote.CreateOpts)


M.template({opts?})                                     *denote.create.template*
     Create a note prompting for template (`denote-template`).

    Parameters: ~
        {opts?}  (denote.CreateOpts)


M.signature({opts?})                                   *denote.create.signature*
     Create a note prompting for signature (`denote-signature`).

    Parameters: ~
        {opts?}  (denote.CreateOpts)


M.open_or_create({opts?})                         *denote.create.open_or_create*
     Open an existing Denote note, or create a new one if no match is selected
     (`denote-open-or-create`).

    Parameters: ~
        {opts?}  (denote.CreateOpts)


                                     *denote.create.open_or_create_with_command*
M.open_or_create_with_command({opts?})
     Open an existing note or choose which creation command to run (`denote-open-or-create-with-command`).

    Parameters: ~
        {opts?}  ({dir?:string})


M.region({opts?})                                         *denote.create.region*
     Create a new Denote note containing the current visual selection (`denote-region`).
     If invoked from a code buffer, wraps the region in an Org `#+begin_src <lang>` or
     Markdown fenced code block matching the target note's syntax.

    Parameters: ~
        {opts?}  (denote.RegionOpts)

denote.CaptureOrigin                                      *denote.CaptureOrigin*

    Fields: ~
        {bufnr?}     (integer)
        {path?}      (string)
        {lnum?}      (integer)

denote.CaptureContext                                    *denote.CaptureContext*

    Fields: ~
        {origin?}        (denote.CaptureOrigin)             Where the capture was started from
        {region?}        (string)                           Text for `%i`
        {answers?}       (table<string,string>)             Prompt answers keyed by prompt name (pre-supplied or collected)
        {prompt_order?}  ({name:string,default?:string}[])  Prompt order shared across title/signature/body backreferences
        {syntax?}        ()


denote.CaptureTemplate                                  *denote.CaptureTemplate*

    Fields: ~
        {key}            (string)                                        Key used by `:Denote capture <key>` and shown in the picker
        {description?}   (string)
        {template?}      (string|fun(ctx:denote.CaptureContext):string)  Body (default: `capture.specifiers`)
        {title?}         (string|fun(ctx:denote.CaptureContext):string)  May contain escapes (e.g. `%^{Title}`)
        {keywords?}      (string[]|string)
        {file_type?}     (string)
        {subdirectory?}  (string)
        {signature?}     (string|fun(ctx:denote.CaptureContext):string)
        {date?}          (string|integer)
        {dir?}           (string)
        {prompts?}       (string[])                                      Denote prompts for fields left unset (default: `config.prompts`)
        {target?}        ()


M.prompts({template?})                                  *denote.capture.prompts*
     Return the distinct prompts of `template` in order of first appearance.

    Parameters: ~
        {template?}  (string)

    Returns: ~
        ({name:string,default?:string}[])


M.ask({templates}, {answers}, {done})                       *denote.capture.ask*
     Ask (asynchronously, via `vim.ui.input`) every `%^{...}` prompt of `templates` that has no
     answer in `answers` yet, then call `done(answers)`. Cancelling a prompt aborts. When nothing
     needs asking (or the prompts complete synchronously), `done`'s result is returned.

    Parameters: ~
        {templates}  (string|nil[])
        {answers}    (table<string,string>)
        {done}       (fun(answers:table<string,string>):any)

    Returns: ~
        (any)


M.syntax_for({file_type?})                           *denote.capture.syntax_for*
     Map a Denote file type to a link syntax.

    Parameters: ~
        {file_type?}  (string)  @return "org"|"markdown"|"text"

M.finalize({content}, {cursor?})                       *denote.capture.finalize*
     Ensure `content` ends with a newline; when `cursor` is at the very end, add an empty line
     for it to land on.

    Parameters: ~
        {content}  (string)
        {cursor?}  (integer)

    Returns: ~
        (string)


M.offset_to_pos({content}, {offset})              *denote.capture.offset_to_pos*

    Parameters: ~
        {content}  (string)
        {offset}   (integer)

    Returns: ~
        (integer[])


M.region_text({bufnr?}, {line1}, {line2})           *denote.capture.region_text*
     Text of lines `line1..line2` of `bufnr`; uses the exact (charwise / blockwise) visual
     selection when the `'<`/`'>` marks match the range.

    Parameters: ~
        {bufnr?}  (integer)
        {line1}   (integer)
        {line2}   (integer)

    Returns: ~
        (string)

    Parameters: ~

M.run({entry}, {ctx}, {opts?})                              *denote.capture.run*
     Run one capture template: create a new note, or append to `entry.target`.

    Parameters: ~

        {ctx}    (denote.CaptureContext)
        {opts?}  ({open?:boolean,how?:string,save?:boolean,interactive?:boolean})

    Returns: ~
        (any)  Created note meta / append result (when no prompt was needed)


M.open_dispatch({list}, {on_pick})                *denote.capture.open_dispatch*
     Open a single-key centered float for capture templates (like Org's capture dispatcher).

    Parameters: ~
        {list}     (denote.CaptureTemplate[])
        {on_pick}  (fun(entry:denote.CaptureTemplate))

    Returns: ~
        (integer)  win


denote.CaptureOpts                                          *denote.CaptureOpts*

    Fields: ~
        {key?}          (string)                  Capture template key (picker when omitted and several are configured)
        {entry?}        (denote.CaptureTemplate)  Use this template directly
        {region?}       (string)                  Text for `%i`
        {line1?}        (integer)                 Take `%i` from lines `line1..line2` of the current buffer
        {line2?}        (integer)
        {answers?}      (table<string,string>)    Pre-supplied prompt answers
        {origin?}       (denote.CaptureOrigin)
        {open?}         (boolean)
        {how?}          (string)
        {save?}         (boolean)
        {interactive?}  (boolean)                 When false, never prompt (prompts use their defaults)

Journal entries (matching `denote-journal`)                     *denote.journal*

M.directory()                                         *denote.journal.directory*
     Return the configured journal directory (defaults to `<denote.directory>/journal` if configured,
     otherwise `<denote.directory>`).

    Returns: ~
        (string)


M.keyword()                                             *denote.journal.keyword*
     Return the journal keyword slug (default: `"journal"`).

    Returns: ~
        (string)


M.interval()                                           *denote.journal.interval*
     Return the configured journal interval (`denote-journal-interval`). Unknown values are
     treated as `"daily"`, like Emacs.
    @return "daily"|"weekly"|"monthly"|"yearly"


M.week_start()                                       *denote.journal.week_start*
     First day of the week: 1 = Monday (ISO 8601, default), 0 = Sunday.

    Returns: ~
        (integer)


M.iso_week()                                           *denote.journal.iso_week*


M.period_bounds()                                 *denote.journal.period_bounds*


M.format_title({ts}, {interval?})                  *denote.journal.format_title*
     Format a journal entry title for Unix timestamp `ts`. `%V`/`%G` are expanded to the
     ISO week number / week-based year portably (also on platforms whose strftime lacks them).

    Parameters: ~
        {ts}         (integer)
        {interval?}  (string)   (default: configured interval)

    Returns: ~
        (string)


M.entries()                                             *denote.journal.entries*
     List all journal entries: Denote files in the journal directory whose keywords include the
     journal keyword (any Denote file when the keyword is empty), sorted by path.

    Returns: ~
        ({path:string,identifier:string,time:integer}[])


M.entries_by_date({opts?})                      *denote.journal.entries_by_date*
     Group journal entries by the day of their identifier.
     With `year`/`month` given, only entries from that month are included.

    Parameters: ~

==============================================================================
Creating, parsing, following, finding, and converting Denote links
                                                                *denote.links*

 Full syntax support for:
 - Org mode:      `[[denote:ID][Description]]`, `[[denote:ID]]`,
                  `[[denote:ID::*Heading][Description]]`, `[[denote:ID::#custom-id][Description]]`,
                  `[[denote:query-contents:QUERY][Description]]`, `[[denote:query-filenames:QUERY][Description]]`
 - Markdown:      `[Description](denote:ID)`, `[Description](denote:ID::#heading-slug)`,
                  `[[denote:ID|Description]]`, `[[denote:ID]]`,
                  `[Description](denote:query-contents:QUERY)`, `[Description](denote:query-filenames:QUERY)`
 - Plain text:    `[[denote:ID][Description]]`, `denote:ID`

denote.Link                                                        *denote.Link*

    Fields: ~
        {kind}          ("id"|"query-contents"|"query-filenames")
        {target}        (string)                                   Raw target after `denote:` (e.g. `20261123T191500` or `20261123T191500::*Heading`)
        {identifier?}   (string)                                   15-char Denote identifier (when kind == "id")
        {search?}       (string)                                   Optional search suffix after `::` (e.g. `*Heading`, `#custom-id`, `/regex/`)
        {query?}        (string)                                   Search query (when kind is query-contents or query-filenames)
        {description?}  (string)                                   Link display text
        {syntax}        ("org"|"markdown"|"wiki"|"plain")
        {start_col}     (integer)                                  1-based inclusive column
        {end_col}       (integer)                                  1-based inclusive column
        {lnum?}         (integer)                                  1-based line number
        {raw}           (string)                                   Full matched link string


M.buffer_syntax({bufnr?})                           *denote.links.buffer_syntax*
     Determine the link syntax to use for a buffer or file path.

    Parameters: ~
        {bufnr?}  (integer)

    Returns: ~
        ("org"|"markdown"|"text")

Backlinks discovery and interactive backlinks buffer          *denote.backlinks*

 Mirrors Emacs `denote-backlinks` and `denote-find-backlink`:
 - Finds every note in the Denote directory referencing the current note's identifier.
 - Works with zero external dependencies (pure Lua scanner) and accelerates with `rg` when available.
 - Opens an interactive split buffer showing file headers + matching context lines
   with `<CR>` to jump, `o` other window, `f` toggle context/filenames-only, `r` refresh, `q` close.

Full-text grep and Denote 4.0 query links                         *denote.query*

 Implements:
 - `grep(query, opts)`: fast full-text search across Denote notes (uses `rg` if installed,
   with pure-Lua fallback so it works with zero external binaries).
 - Interactive `*Denote query*` buffer matching Emacs `denote-query-mode`:
   `<CR>` jump, `o` other window, `f` narrow/filter, `x` exclude matches, `c` clear filters,
   `r` refresh, `q` close.
 - `query_contents_link` (`denote-query-contents-link`): inserts `denote:query-contents:...`
 - `query_filenames_link` (`denote-query-filenames-link`): inserts `denote:query-filenames:...`

        {text}  (string)

     Search contents of Denote text files in `dir` (or explicit `opts.files`) matching `query`.
     Uses `rg` when available with a pure-Lua fallback so it works with zero external binaries
     (see `denote.search`). Pass `on_done` to search asynchronously.

    Parameters: ~
        {query}     (string)
        {opts?}     ({dir?:string,files?:string[],file_regexp?:string,case_sensitive?:boolean,fixed?:boolean})
        {on_done?}  (fun(matches:denote.GrepMatch[]))

    Returns: ~
        (denote.GrepMatch[]|denote.SearchHandle)


M.grep({query?}, {opts?})                                    *denote.query.grep*
     Open the interactive Denote grep / query results buffer (`denote-grep`).
     Supports all Denote 4.3.1 query refinement commands:
       f: include files matching regexp (`denote-query-only-include-files`)
       x: exclude files matching regexp (`denote-query-exclude-files`)
       k: include files with keyword(s) (`denote-query-only-include-files-with-keywords`)
       K: exclude files with keyword(s) (`denote-query-exclude-files-with-keywords`)
       /: focus search — grep new query only in currently matched files (`denote-query-focus-last-search`)
       S: sort matched files by component (`denote-query-sort-last-search`)
       c: clear all filters (`denote-query-clear-all-filters`)

    Parameters: ~
        {query?}  (string)
        {opts?}   ({dir?:string,files?:string[],file_regexp?:string})


                                  *denote.query.grep_files_referenced_in_region*

==============================================================================
Shared full-text search engine (ripgrep with pure-Lua fallback)  *denote.search*

 Every content search in denote.nvim (grep, query links, backlinks, unlinked mentions)
 goes through `M.run`, so results are consistent no matter which backend runs:

 - `rg` is used when installed (`search.ripgrep = true`), always with `--no-ignore --hidden`
   so `.gitignore`d or dot-directories never hide notes. Candidates are always filtered by the
   Denote file index, so excluded directories/files behave the same as in the Lua path.
 - Exit code 1 ("no matches") is a valid empty result, not a reason to rescan in Lua.
 - Loaded buffers with unsaved changes are searched from the buffer, not from disk.
 - Case handling is the same everywhere: "smart" (default) is case-insensitive unless the
   pattern contains an uppercase letter.
 - Regex dialect: Rust regex with `rg`, Vim "very magic" (`\v`) without it. Both treat
   `| ( ) + ? {n}` as operators, so common patterns behave the same.

 Pass a callback to run asynchronously (UI never blocks); omit it to get results directly.

denote.SearchMatch                                          *denote.SearchMatch*

    Fields: ~
        {file}  (string)   Absolute path
        {lnum}  (integer)  1-based line number
        {col}   (integer)  1-based byte column of the first match on the line
        {text}  (string)   Trimmed line text


denote.SearchSpec                                            *denote.SearchSpec*

    Fields: ~
        {pattern}  (string)                             Regex (or literal string with `fixed = true`)
        {files}    (string[])                           Candidate files (only matches inside these are returned)
        {fixed?}   (boolean)                            Treat `pattern` as a literal string
        {word?}    (boolean)                            Require word boundaries around matches
        {case?}    ("smart"|"sensitive"|"insensitive")  Default "smart"
        {root?}    (string)                             Directory to hand to `rg` when there are many candidates


M.use_ripgrep()                                      *denote.search.use_ripgrep*
     Return true when ripgrep should be used.

    Returns: ~
        (boolean)


M.reset()                                                  *denote.search.reset*
     Reset the cached `rg` executable check (tests / PATH changes).


M.matcher({spec})                                        *denote.search.matcher*
     Build a line matcher for the pure-Lua path. Returns fun(line): col|nil.

    Parameters: ~
        {spec}  (denote.SearchSpec)

    Returns: ~
        (fun(line:string):integer|nil)


denote.SearchHandle                                        *denote.SearchHandle*

    Fields: ~
        {cancel}  (fun())


M.run({spec}, {on_done?})                                    *denote.search.run*
     Run a search. With `on_done`, runs asynchronously and returns a handle; otherwise blocks
     and returns the matches.

    Parameters: ~
        {spec}      (denote.SearchSpec)
        {on_done?}  (fun(matches:denote.SearchMatch[]))

    Returns: ~
        (denote.SearchMatch[]|denote.SearchHandle)


==============================================================================
Hover preview of the note behind a `denote:` link               *denote.preview*

 `:Denote preview` (default buffer-local `K` on a link) opens a floating window with the
 target note's title, identifier, keywords, and the first lines of its body (starting at the
 linked heading for `denote:ID::#heading` / `::*Heading` links). Press `K` again to focus the
 float, `q` / `<Esc>` inside it to close, or `<CR>` to open the note.

M.build({path}, {search?})                                *denote.preview.build*
     Build the preview lines for the note at `path`.

    Parameters: ~
        {path}     (string)
        {search?}  (string)

    Returns: ~
        (string[])  lines
        (string)    filetype

     Close the preview window if open.

        {link?}  (denote.Link)

    Returns: ~
        (integer|nil)  win


==============================================================================
Vault-wide reports: unlinked mentions, broken links, orphan notes
                                                               *denote.report*

 - `:Denote unlinked_mentions` lists every line in other notes that mentions the current
   note's title without linking to it (quickfix list). Jump to one and run
   `:Denote link_mention` to turn that mention into a `denote:` link.
 - `:Denote check` scans all notes and fills the quickfix list with broken `denote:` links
   and orphan notes (notes no other note links to).

M.last_mention_target                        *denote.report.last_mention_target*
     Target of the last `unlinked_mentions` run (used by `link_mention`).

    Type: ~
        ({path:string,identifier:string,title:string}|nil)

        {opts?}     ({file?:string,quickfix?:boolean,sync?:boolean})
        {on_done?}  (fun(matches:denote.SearchMatch[]))

    Returns: ~
        (denote.SearchMatch[]|denote.SearchHandle|nil)


M.link_mention({target?})                           *denote.report.link_mention*
     Replace the first unlinked mention of the last `unlinked_mentions` target on the current line
     with a `denote:` link (description keeps the text exactly as written).

    Parameters: ~
        {target?}  ({identifier:string,title:string,path?:string})

    Returns: ~
        (boolean)


denote.CheckReport                                          *denote.CheckReport*

    Fields: ~
        {broken}   ({file:string,lnum:integer,col:integer,identifier:string}[])
        {orphans}  (string[])                                                    Notes no other note links to

     Scan every note for broken links and orphans.
     Without `on_done` returns the report directly; with it, runs asynchronously.

    Parameters: ~
        {opts?}     ({quickfix?:boolean,orphans?:boolean,sync?:boolean})
        {on_done?}  (fun(report:denote.CheckReport))

    Returns: ~
        (denote.CheckReport|denote.SearchHandle)


==============================================================================
Renaming Denote files and syncing front matter                   *denote.rename*

 Supports two-way synchronization between Denote filenames and front matter:
 - `rename_file`: rename ANY file (including PDFs, images, non-Denote files) into
   Denote's naming scheme and optionally update/add front matter.
 - `rename_file_title`, `rename_file_keywords`, `rename_file_signature`, `rename_file_date`
 - `rename_file_using_front_matter`: sync filename on disk from edits inside front matter.
 - `add_front_matter`: prepend Denote front matter to a note lacking it.
 - `keywords_add` / `keywords_remove`: quick keyword edits.
 - `format_buffer_name` / `statusline`: Denote rename-buffer display formatting.

M.is_renaming({bufnr})                               *denote.rename.is_renaming*
     Return true when `bufnr` is currently being written by `denote.rename`.

    Parameters: ~
        {bufnr}  (integer)

    Returns: ~
        (boolean)


denote.RenameOpts                                            *denote.RenameOpts*

    Fields: ~
        {file?}                  (string)           Target file path (default: current buffer)
        {title?}                 (string)           New title (pass "" to remove title)
        {keywords?}              (string[]|string)  New keywords (pass {} to remove keywords)
        {signature?}             (string)           New signature (pass "" to remove signature)
        {identifier?}            (string)           New identifier (keeps existing or generates from mtime/now)
        {date?}                  (string|integer)   New date (recomputes identifier)
        {rewrite_front_matter?}  (boolean)          Default true for supported text file types
        {add_front_matter?}      (boolean)          Add front matter if missing (default false)

        {opts}  (denote.RenameOpts)

        (string|nil)  err

M.format_buffer_name({bufnr?}, {fmt?})        *denote.rename.format_buffer_name*
     Format a human-friendly buffer label (matching `denote-rename-buffer-format`).
     Specifiers:
       %t  front matter title (or filename title)
       %T  filename title (desluggified)
       %i  identifier (`YYYYMMDDTHHMMSS`)
       %I  human date from identifier (`Mon, 23 Nov 2026`)
       %d  identifier (DATE mnemonic, same as %i)
       %D  DWIM: %t if non-empty, else %I, else %i (upstream default)
       %s  signature
       %k  keywords
       %b  backlinks indicator (`rename_buffer_backlinks_indicator`) if note has backlinks
       %%  literal `%`

    Parameters: ~
        {bufnr?}  (integer)
        {fmt?}    (string)

    Returns: ~
        (string)


==============================================================================
Front matter generation, parsing, and in-place rewriting    *denote.frontmatter*

 Supports all four canonical Emacs Denote file types:
 - `org` (`.org`): `#+title:`, `#+date:`, `#+filetags:`, `#+identifier:`, `#+signature:`
 - `markdown-yaml` (`.md`): YAML front matter delimited by `---`
 - `markdown-toml` (`.md`): TOML front matter delimited by `+++`
 - `text` (`.txt`): plain text key/value header terminated by `---------------------------`
 Plus user-defined custom file types in `config.opts.file_types`.

     Return all configured file types (built-ins merged with user overrides).

    Returns: ~
        (table<string,table>)

==============================================================================
Denote file-naming scheme, parser, sluggifier, and identifier generator
                                                               *denote.naming*

 Implements the canonical Emacs Denote file-naming scheme:
   DATE==SIGNATURE--TITLE__KEYWORDS.EXTENSION
 as well as Denote 3.x/4.x reordered components (`@@DATE` when identifier is not first),
 partial Denote filenames, compound extensions (e.g. `.org.gpg`), sluggification,
 desluggification, and collision-free identifier generation.

     Remove excluded punctuation from `str`.

        {str}  (string)

    Returns: ~
        (string)

==============================================================================
Fast directory scanning, file lookup, and keyword discovery       *denote.files*

denote.IndexEntry                                            *denote.IndexEntry*
     In-memory index of directory trees, keyed by root.

     Each entry holds every (non-excluded) file below the root plus the mtime of every
     directory that was scanned. Adding, removing, or renaming an entry changes the mtime of
     its parent directory, so validating an entry only needs one `stat` per directory instead
     of a full recursive `scandir`. Operations performed by denote.nvim itself also call
     `M.invalidate()` explicitly (covers filesystems with coarse mtime resolution).

    Fields: ~
        {files}          (string[])               Sorted absolute paths
        {dirs}           (table<string,string>)   Directory path -> mtime key
        {ids?}           (table<string,string>)   Identifier -> first path (built lazily)
        {denote?}        (table<string,boolean>)  Path -> is a Denote file (built lazily)
        {text?}          (table<string,boolean>)  Path -> has a text note extension (built lazily)
        {validated_at?}  (integer)                Loop time (`uv.now()`) of the last freshness check


M.touch()                                                   *denote.files.touch*
     Signal that note *contents* changed (e.g. a buffer was saved) without forcing a rescan of
     directory listings. Content-derived caches (backlink indicators) refresh on next use.


M.invalidate({dir?})                                   *denote.files.invalidate*
     Drop cached directory listings (all roots, or only `dir`).

    Parameters: ~
        {dir?}  (string)


M.is_text_file({path}, {exts?})                      *denote.files.is_text_file*
     Return true if `path` has a text note extension (`.org`, `.md`, `.txt`, or a custom file type).

    Parameters: ~
        {path}   (string)

    Returns: ~
        (boolean)

==============================================================================
Folgezettel / hierarchical sequence notes (matching `denote-sequence`)
                                                             *denote.sequence*

 Supports both sequence schemes from Emacs `denote-sequence`:
 - `"numeric"`:      `1`, `2`, `1=1`, `1=2`, `1=1=1`
 - `"alphanumeric"`: `1`, `2`, `1a`, `1b`, `1a1`, `1a2`, `1a1a`

 Provides:
 - `new_parent`, `new_child`, `new_sibling`
 - `relatives` / `find_relatives` (parent, children, siblings, all)
 - `find` / `link` / `reparent`

M.scheme()                                              *denote.sequence.scheme*
     Return the active sequence scheme ("numeric" or "alphanumeric").

    Returns: ~
        ("numeric"|"alphanumeric")


M.split({sig}, {scheme?})                                *denote.sequence.split*
     Split a sequence signature into depth segments.
     Numeric: `"1=2=1"` -> `{ "1", "2", "1" }`
     Alphanumeric: `"1a2b"` -> `{ "1", "a", "2", "b" }`

    Parameters: ~
        {sig}      (string)
        {scheme?}  ("numeric"|"alphanumeric")

    Returns: ~
        (string[])


M.join({parts}, {scheme?})                                *denote.sequence.join*
     Join sequence segments back into a signature string.

    Parameters: ~
        {parts}    (string[])
        {scheme?}  ("numeric"|"alphanumeric")

    Returns: ~
        (string)


M.is_valid({sig}, {scheme?})                          *denote.sequence.is_valid*
     Check whether `sig` is a valid sequence signature under `scheme`.

    Parameters: ~
        {sig}      (string|nil)

    Returns: ~
        (boolean)

     Return relatives of `sig` in `dir`:
     `{ parent = path|nil, children = path[], siblings = path[], descendants = path[] }`.

    Parameters: ~
        {sig}   (string)
        {dir?}  (string)

    Returns: ~
        ({parent:string|nil,children:string[],siblings:string[],descendants:string[]})


M.new_parent({opts?})                               *denote.sequence.new_parent*
     Create a new top-level sequence note (`denote-sequence-new-parent`).

    Parameters: ~
        {opts?}  (denote.CreateOpts)


denote.SequenceCreateOpts : denote.CreateOpts        *denote.SequenceCreateOpts*

    Fields: ~
        {parent_signature?}   (string)   Parent sequence for `new_child` (prompted when absent)
        {sibling_signature?}  (string)   Sibling sequence for `new_sibling` (prompted when absent)
        {pick?}               (boolean)  Always pick the base note with a picker


M.new_child({opts?})                                 *denote.sequence.new_child*
     Create a child sequence note (`denote-sequence-new-child`).

    Parameters: ~
        {opts?}  (denote.SequenceCreateOpts)

    Returns: ~
        (table|nil)

     Create a sibling sequence note (`denote-sequence-new-sibling`).

    Parameters: ~
        {opts?}  (denote.SequenceCreateOpts)

    Returns: ~
        (table|nil)

     Pick and open a sequence note (`denote-sequence-find`).

    Parameters: ~
        {opts?}  ({dir?:string})


M.find_relatives({opts?})                       *denote.sequence.find_relatives*

     (`denote-sequence-find-relatives-dired` / `denote-sequence-find-next-sibling`).

     Insert a link to a sequence note (`denote-sequence-link`).

M.reparent({opts?})                                   *denote.sequence.reparent*
     Reparent the current note under a chosen parent sequence (`denote-sequence-reparent`).
     When `recursive` is true (or confirmed interactively), descendants are also renumbered.

    Parameters: ~
        {opts?}  ({file?:string,parent_signature?:string,dir?:string,recursive?:boolean})


==============================================================================
Isolated Denote silos (matching `denote-silo`)                     *denote.silo*

 Allows keeping separate, self-contained Denote note repositories (e.g. work vs personal)
 configured via `config.opts.silos` or discovered via `.denote.lua` / `.denote.json`
 directory-local config files (Neovim counterpart of Emacs `.dir-locals.el` silos).

M.list()                                                      *denote.silo.list*
     Return all configured silos (normalized) plus the primary directory.

    Returns: ~
        (string[])


M.detect({path?})                                           *denote.silo.detect*
     Walk upward from `path` (default: current buffer path) looking for a `.denote.lua`
     or `.denote.json` marker file, or checking if `path` is inside one of `config.opts.silos`.
     Returns the silo root directory and optional local config overrides table.

    Parameters: ~
        {path?}  (string)

    Returns: ~
        (string|nil)  dir
        (table|nil)   local_opts


M.with_silo({silo_dir}, {fn})                            *denote.silo.with_silo*
     Run a function `fn` with `config.active_directory` temporarily bound to `silo_dir`
     (and any `.denote.json`/`.denote.lua` local overrides applied).

    Parameters: ~
        {silo_dir}  (string)
        {fn}        (fun():any)

    Returns: ~
        (any)


M.switch({silo_dir?})                                       *denote.silo.switch*
     Switch the active Denote directory for this session (applying any `.denote.json` / trusted
     `.denote.lua` overrides on top of the base configuration).

    Parameters: ~
        {silo_dir?}  (string)  Pass nil to reset to default `config.opts.directory`


M.pick({callback}, {title?})                                  *denote.silo.pick*
     Pick a silo interactively and invoke `callback(silo_dir)`.

    Parameters: ~
        {callback}  (fun(silo_dir:string))
        {title?}    (string)


M.create_note({silo_dir?})                             *denote.silo.create_note*
     Create a note in a chosen silo (`denote-silo-create-note`).

    Parameters: ~
        {silo_dir?}  (string)


M.open_or_create({silo_dir?})                       *denote.silo.open_or_create*
     Open or create a note in a chosen silo (`denote-silo-open-or-create`).

    Parameters: ~
        {silo_dir?}  (string)


M.explorer({silo_dir?})                                   *denote.silo.explorer*
     Open the Denote Explorer in a chosen silo (`denote-silo-dired`).

    Parameters: ~
        {silo_dir?}  (string)
